# SK2014 — An empty catch silently discards an exception

<!-- Generated from Rules/Rikarin.Skala.Rules.Metadata/rules.json. Do not edit. -->

A filterless catch block contains no statement or explanation.

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | Correctness |
| Default severity | warning |
| Scope | Syntax |
| Needs a compilation | no |
| Fix | no |
| Language version floor | — |
| Since | 2.0 |

## Why

An empty catch converts an exceptional path into apparent success and erases the only evidence of the failure. If ignoring an exception is deliberate, the code should say why; otherwise it should handle, log or propagate it.

## Example

Instead of:

```csharp
try { Save(); } catch (IOException) { }
```

Write:

```csharp
try { Save(); } catch (IOException ex) { Log(ex); throw; }
```

## When it does not fire

Only a truly empty, uncommented, filterless catch is reported. A comment is accepted as an explicit justification, a filter documents which exceptional condition is intentionally accepted, and any statement means the exception is not silently swallowed. No automatic fix can infer the intended recovery policy.

## Configuration

- `dotnet_diagnostic.SK2014.severity`
